rationale: Interpret receipt f64ce69f57134681b38e73bed2fd137e, which resolves the gap the last account named. The grown phantom configuration {A,B,C} does admit a quorum that omits a committed voter: after the failed AddVoter(C), with C reachable and the other committed voter partitioned, the leader re-elected with its own vote plus C's and committed a client command at index 4 while the committed voter's log ended at 2. The control, with C also cut, produced no re-election and no commit, so the acknowledgement that carried the commit came from the server the committed configuration does not contain. This refutes the previous boundary claim that an unsupported commit needs a failed removal, and it also refutes the older reading that a grown phantom quorum necessarily contains a committed majority. The interpretation is rewritten accordingly; the conclusion and the asserted defect are unchanged, and the earlier shrink receipts keep their independent support. One comparison in the new receipt is unevaluated because its asserted field was emitted on the case event rather than the result event; that is a definition defect in this experiment, recorded as a limitation, and the case event itself carries the error.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry with dispatchLogs and then, regardless of whether the entry was stored, sets the latest configuration to the new configuration at the index the entry would have occupied, reconfigures the commitment map and restarts replication; dispatchLogs answers the futures with the store error and moves the node to follower, leaving the in-memory latest configuration ahead of the stored log.
knowledge.conditions: Leader applying a configuration change whose StoreLogs call fails.

knowledge.statement: quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all derive their voter set and quorum from the node's latest configuration, so a latest configuration that is not present in the log governs elections and commitment for that node.
knowledge.conditions: Any node whose configurations.latest refers to an unstored configuration entry.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. A configuration change whose log write fails is reported to the caller as failed, but the new configuration is nevertheless installed in the leader's in-memory latest configuration at the index the entry would have occupied. The node then treats that unstored configuration as authoritative for two separate decisions: whom it counts as a voter and whom it asks for votes. Evidence from receipt 0e6dd623c01e43a4b9e33cafc544ecf2 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0). Parsed index 0, the case event: two voters were bootstrapped, the leader's store failed exactly the configuration write, and afterwards latest_index_after_fail=3 with last_log_index_after_fail=2, while phantom_servers records the shrunken configuration containing only the leader itself. Parsed index 1, the result: remove_failed=true with remove_error 'injected store failure', latest_index_exceeds_log=true, re_elected=true, apply_ok=true, commit_index=4, leader_last_index=4 and peer_last_index=2, so commit_without_peer=true. Under the committed two-voter configuration a quorum is both members, so the command the client was told had committed at index 4 never reached a quorum of that configuration. Mechanism from source: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, unconditionally, calls setLatestConfiguration with the new configuration at the dispatched index, reconfigures the commitment map and restarts replication (raft.go:1204-1244), while dispatchLogs' store-error path only answers the futures with the error and moves the node to follower (raft.go:1245-1296). quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all read that latest configuration (raft.go:1087-1100, 1999-2071, 456-468), and startStopReplication opens a stream to every configured server (raft.go:583-600), so the phantom configuration governs the election the node wins, the quorum it uses to commit, and the set of servers whose acknowledgements it collects. The restart phase of receipt 76bdaf3e107643d4a3ed1247faa52460 is withdrawn as evidence: that harness created a fresh in-memory transport for the restarted node without connecting it to the other member's transport, so the restarted node could not reach the peer at all, and its restarted_as_leader=false and unchanged peer log index are explained by the missing wiring. The target's own membership document states the condition this violates: a new configuration 'will be in affect as soon as it is appended to the log' (membership.md:15). In the failed-write case nothing was appended, so the condition the document sets for a configuration to take effect was never met, yet the node used the new voter set for its election and for committing. Shrink direction, four receipts: after a failed RemoveServer the phantom configuration contains only the leader and the later command commits with commit_without_peer=true in 0e6dd623c01e43a4b9e33cafc544ecf2 (parsed index 1), in the corrected restart revision adbbb5d29a08477b9dbbd7da187f7f26 (parsed index 1), in the shrink case of the two-direction control 99292afefb9d4308957a0e2d150bf11d (parsed index 1) and in the clean-copy repeat e7a4c652bb2b4273972d661adccd41e9 (parsed index 1), with the leader and removed follower roles covered in both assignments across those receipts. Recovery after the lone commit was observed in two of them (adbbb5d29a08477b9dbbd7da187f7f26 parsed index 2, e7a4c652bb2b4273972d661adccd41e9 parsed index 2): the restarted node led again and the peer's log reached the index the lone commit had occupied. Grown direction, now decisive: receipt f64ce69f57134681b38e73bed2fd137e (completed, tests_passed, exit 0) runs three real nodes, bootstraps {A,B} as the committed voter set and starts C with no configuration, so the membership guards in requestVote that test a non-empty server list do not reject the leader (raft.go:1696-1707). Parsed index 0, the reachable case event: AddVoter('C') failed with the injected store error, latest_index_after_fail=3 against last_log_index_after_fail=2, and phantom_servers records {A,B,C} with three voters. Parsed index 1, the reachable case result: after the leader was partitioned from B and left connected to C, re_elected=true, apply_ok=true, commit_index=4 with leader_last_index=4 and new_server_last_index=4, while committed_peer_last_index=2, so committed_peer_has_entry=false and commit_without_committed_voter=true. The leader therefore regained office on its own vote plus C's, and reached the commit quorum of two with its own acknowledgement plus C's, while the single committed voter other than itself never received the entry. Parsed index 2, the control case event: the same failed write left the same three-voter phantom configuration. Parsed index 3, the control result: with both B and C unreachable, re_elected=false, apply_ok=false with the apply refused as 'node is not the leader', commit_index=2 and new_server_last_index=0, so no command committed. Cutting C is what removed the second vote and the second acknowledgement, which is what makes C the supplier of the support that produced the trigger's commit. Consequence under the exercised conditions: after a transient failure to store a configuration change, a node can adopt a voter set the rest of the cluster never accepted, win an election with the vote of a server that is not in the committed configuration, and report a client command committed while the committed voters hold different logs. The earlier statement that this needs a failed removal, and the earlier statement that a grown phantom quorum necessarily retains a committed majority, are both refuted: the grown configuration {A,B,C} admits {A,C}, and when that pair was reachable it produced exactly the unsupported commit the shrink direction produces.

knowledge.assertion: appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration in memory regardless of whether its log entry was stored.
quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState derive voter sets from the latest configuration.

counterevidence: The phantom state does not outlive a restart in the shrink configuration: in receipts adbbb5d29a08477b9dbbd7da187f7f26 and e7a4c652bb2b4273972d661adccd41e9 the restarted node led again and the peer's log reached the same index, so an entry first committed alone later became a quorum commit of the committed configuration. The durability hazard is confined to the interval between that lone commit and a successful restart with the peer reachable.

The commit without a quorum of the committed configuration required the store to fail once and then succeed: the harness fails a single StoreLogs call, and a persistent write failure would also block the later client command, so the exercised trigger is a transient store error rather than a permanent one.

The hazard needs a committed voter to be unreachable at the time of the commit. In the grown case of receipt 99292afefb9d4308957a0e2d150bf11d the other committed voter stayed reachable and held the committed index, and in the clean-copy repeat e7a4c652bb2b4273972d661adccd41e9 no command committed at all; only with that voter partitioned, in receipt f64ce69f57134681b38e73bed2fd137e, did the phantom quorum produce an unsupported commit.

C held the entries the phantom leader sent it (new_server_last_index=4 in receipt f64ce69f57134681b38e73bed2fd137e), but nothing recorded C's own view of its role: it was started with no configuration, so the events show it stored entries and granted a vote, not that it behaved as an acknowledged member of the cluster.

The other committed voter keeps the committed view and cannot win an election while the phantom leader is alive and reachable, so the two nodes do not both claim leadership; the harness observed the leader's side and C's log, and did not measure how long the committed voter stays unable to win.
limitations: The grown-quorum receipt contains one run of each case, so the reachable-new-server shape has been observed once; the shrink direction, by contrast, has four receipts. Repetition of the grown case, and a case where the added server carries its own configuration, were not exercised.

The partition is applied after the failed configuration write. A partition that exists when the write fails, or that heals during the apply window, is not exercised, and the harness does not distinguish a partition that blocks votes from one that blocks replication only.

The added server is a raft node with an empty log, empty stable store and no configuration; a real deployment's new server may already hold state or configuration, which would change how it answers votes and appends.
The client-visible completion point was the Apply future returning nil; no read path through the FSM was exercised.

One comparison in receipt f64ce69f57134681b38e73bed2fd137e is unevaluated: it asserted add_failed on the result event while the harness emitted that field only on the case event, so the receipt reports the admission check as unknown. The case event itself records add_error 'injected store failure' with failure_injected=true, and the draft harness now emits add_failed on both events so a re-execution would evaluate it.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipt adbbb5d29a08477b9dbbd7da187f7f26 is the third revision of 6491640ed49a4c7b8f5150438d350e36-experiment under this question and replaces the restart phase of the second revision, whose transport wiring was defective; the failed change, the phantom configuration and the lone commit are identical across the first and third receipts, so they describe the same subject. Receipt 99292afefb9d4308957a0e2d150bf11d is the fourth revision of that experiment and adds the grow-direction control, whose shrink case reproduces the earlier outcome. Receipt e7a4c652bb2b4273972d661adcdc41e9 is a clean-copy repeat of that fourth revision from retained inputs, with the same case suffixes; its shrink events match field for field and its grow events diverge only in the commit phase. Receipt f64ce69f57134681b38e73bed2fd137e comes from a separate experiment identifier, 94c20e41b2ad4cfba9d46911ecede913-experiment, created to test the quorum {A,C} that the earlier grow cases could not reach because their added member had no transport. It is recorded here because it intervenes on the same mechanism under the same question: the same failed configuration write, the same latest-configuration adoption, and the same measurement of whether a client command commits without the committed voter. Its case and result events carry the same fields as the b5bd70f5750b4b45af3e925bd1748aaf-experiment events apart from the added new_server fields, so the two bodies of evidence can be read together, and its control differs only by cutting the added server as well.
